partner_context.their_ambition: Grab is deepening its super-app lead in Vietnam — ride-hail, delivery, financial services — across the country's fast-urbanizing, congestion-bound metros, with mobility innovation a core differentiator.
partner_context.their_pressure: Ho Chi Minh City and Hanoi road congestion is worsening faster than infrastructure can absorb, and the marquee coastal-tourism destinations are served by undifferentiated diesel boats — both a ceiling on the urban mobility experience and an unmonetized premium-tourism flow.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: A foiling water-mobility tier bookable in-app: a Saigon River commuter spine that skips the gridlock, a Vung Tau line-haul revival, and premium island-hopping at Ha Long, Da Nang and Phu Quoc — congestion-beating and tourism-monetizing mobility on rivers and coasts Grab already serves on land.

markets.why_now: The Saigon Waterbus and the legacy Vung Tau hydrofoil corridor both proved the demand; HCMC congestion is at a breaking point; and Vietnam's coastal-tourism boom (Quang Ninh alone drew ~19M visitors in 2024) is straining the diesel day-boat fleet. The water layer is ready to be switched on.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open ocean and the berths and jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way, no tunnels or tracks. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all. That's the fundamental contrast with flying taxis and other new-infrastructure modes: nothing to permit, build, or wait for.
why_navier_now.the_moment: The Saigon Waterbus and the legacy Vung Tau hydrofoil corridor both proved the demand; HCMC congestion is at a breaking point; and Vietnam's coastal-tourism boom is straining the diesel day-boat fleet. The water layer is ready to be switched on.

markets.multimodal_fit: Grab's app already routes the first/last mile by car and bike across HCMC, Da Nang, Ha Long and Phu Quoc — the foiling pier becomes the water node in that same trip graph: Grab to the wharf, foil across the river or to the island, Grab onward.

proof_points.claim: Grab is Vietnam's super-app.
proof_points.evidence: Deep ride-hail, delivery and payments penetration across HCMC, Hanoi, Da Nang and the coastal cities gives the demand layer for both urban river commuting and premium island-hopping.

proof_points.claim: HCMC congestion is at a breaking point.
proof_points.evidence: A ~9M-person city (greater metro ~13M) bisected by the Saigon River, with a tiny share of trips on the water despite chronic gridlock.

proof_points.claim: Water-transit demand is already proven.
proof_points.evidence: The Saigon Waterbus (since 2017) and the historic Saigon↔Vung Tau hydrofoil corridor both demonstrated latent commuter and leisure demand on diesel craft.

proof_points.claim: Coastal tourism is booming and under-served.
proof_points.evidence: Quang Ninh (Ha Long) drew ~19M visitors in 2024; Da Nang and Phu Quoc draw millions more — all on slow diesel day-boats with no premium foiling tier.

objections.concern: The Saigon River has tides, current and wet-season debris.
objections.response: Foils ride above the surface chop; software-defined routing flexes with tide and conditions, and the Saigon Waterbus has already proven year-round river operability on the same corridor.

objections.concern: The Vung Tau and island legs are long open-water runs.
objections.response: Quanta-LR is purpose-built for these legs — 2,000 nm hybrid range, no charging dependence — while Pioneer II covers the sheltered river and intra-island hops.

objections.concern: Inland-waterway passenger licensing is complex.
objections.response: The Saigon Waterbus is an established licensing template under Vinamarine and the HCMC Department of Transport; we build on the proven regulatory path rather than a greenfield one.

phases.label: Phase 1 — Saigon River activation (Pioneer II)
phases.narrative: Switch on the Saigon River as a commuter highway — Bach Dang to Thu Thiem, Thanh Da and Thu Duc — a silent zero-wake foiling spine that skips the gridlocked bridges, bookable in the Grab app, in one of the world's most congestion-bound megacities.
phases.rationale: Huge captive congestion demand and an under-used river with a proven water-bus precedent.

phases.label: Phase 2 — Saigon ↔ Vung Tau line-haul (Quanta-LR)
phases.narrative: Revive the historic Saigon↔Vung Tau corridor as a fast clean Quanta-LR hybrid line-haul (~60 nm) — beach-bound weekenders and offshore commuters in roughly half the catamaran time, with no charging-infrastructure dependence at the Vung Tau end. The flagship long-range run that proves intercity water mobility in Vietnam.
phases.rationale: A famous, proven corridor running today on legacy diesel — the natural Quanta-LR showcase.

phases.label: Phase 3 — Coastal island-hopping (Pioneer II + Quanta-LR)
phases.narrative: Extend the water layer to Vietnam's marquee coastal destinations — Da Nang↔Hoi An↔Cham Islands, Ha Long/Lan Ha karst island-hopping, and Phu Quoc↔An Thoi — putting premium foiling island-hopping in-app and replacing the slow diesel day-boat fleet, with Quanta-LR linking the longer coastal legs.
phases.rationale: A booming coastal-tourism market with no premium foiling tier and a ready in-app audience.

end_state.headline: The water layer of Grab's Vietnam super-app — rivers and islands, in-app.
end_state.addressable_footprint: HCMC + Hanoi/Ha Long + Da Nang + Phu Quoc + Nha Trang + the Mekong Delta — Vietnam's congestion-bound metros and marquee coastal destinations.
end_state.narrative: Starting from the Saigon River commuter spine, Grab activates Vietnam's water as a first-class super-app mode: a megacity river highway, a revived Vung Tau line-haul, and premium island-hopping across Ha Long, Da Nang and Phu Quoc — congestion-beating and tourism-monetizing mobility, clean and silent, bookable in the app Vietnamese users already live in.
